explanation_en: A fundamental contrastive prepositional phrase meaning 'instead of' or 'rather than'. It is followed by an infinitive verb or a noun. It is essential for B2/C1 learners to express alternatives and preferences naturally, replacing more repetitive structures.

examples.en_text: Instead of drinking coffee at night, I prefer to have a chamomile tea.
examples.target_text: Em vez de beber café à noite, prefiro tomar um chá de camomila.

examples.en_text: Today I decided to walk to work instead of going by car.
examples.target_text: Hoje decidi ir a pé para o trabalho em vez de ir de carro.

examples.en_text: Instead of arguing, we should try to find a solution together.
examples.target_text: Em vez de discutirmos, devíamos tentar encontrar uma solução juntos.

examples.en_text: He preferred to watch a movie instead of studying for tomorrow's exam.
examples.target_text: Ele preferiu ver um filme em vez de estudar para o exame de amanhã.

examples.en_text: Instead of buying a new car, she decided to save money for the trip.
examples.target_text: Em vez de comprar um carro novo, ela decidiu poupar dinheiro para a viagem.

examples.en_text: Since it was raining, we stayed home instead of going to the park.
examples.target_text: Como estava a chover, ficámos em casa em vez de ir ao parque.

explanation_en: This verb phrase means to turn to a specific measure, help, or source, especially as a solution to a problem. It requires the preposition 'a' (which often merges into 'à' or 'ao'). It is a high-frequency, elegant verb used in medical, legal, and everyday contexts.

examples.en_text: If the fever doesn't go away, we have to turn to a doctor.
examples.target_text: Se a febre não passar, temos de recorrer a um médico.

examples.en_text: They didn't want to borrow money, but they had to resort to the bank.
examples.target_text: Eles não queriam pedir dinheiro emprestado, mas tiveram de recorrer ao banco.

examples.en_text: When I don't know a word in English, I usually turn to the dictionary.
examples.target_text: Quando não sei uma palavra em inglês, costumo recorrer ao dicionário.

examples.en_text: To solve the contract problem, we had to resort to a lawyer.
examples.target_text: Para resolver o problema do contrato, tivemos de recorrer a um advogado.

examples.en_text: You don't need to resort to violence to solve your problems.
examples.target_text: Não precisas de recorrer à violência para resolver os teus problemas.

examples.en_text: Since the exam was very difficult, she had to resort to her classmates' help.
examples.target_text: Como o exame era muito difícil, ela teve de recorrer à ajuda dos colegas.

explanation_en: A very common verb-preposition collocation meaning 'to choose to' or 'to opt for'. It is almost always followed by an infinitive verb or a noun phrase. It is a more formal and precise alternative to 'escolher' or 'decidir'.

examples.en_text: He opted to study engineering instead of medicine.
examples.target_text: Ele optou por estudar engenharia em vez de medicina.

examples.en_text: Since the traffic was bad, she opted to go by subway.
examples.target_text: Como o trânsito estava ruim, ela optou por ir de metrô.

examples.en_text: The company opted to cancel the project due to high costs.
examples.target_text: A empresa optou por cancelar o projeto devido aos custos altos.

examples.en_text: She opted for a vegetarian dish at dinner yesterday.
examples.target_text: Ela optou por um prato vegetariano no jantar de ontem.

examples.en_text: My friend opted to stay in a hotel near the beach.
examples.target_text: O meu amigo optou por ficar num hotel perto da praia.

examples.en_text: After thinking a lot, he opted to sell his old car.
examples.target_text: Depois de pensar muito, ele optou por vender o carro antigo.

explanation_en: An idiomatic expression meaning to disclaim responsibility for something, similar to 'washing one's hands of' a situation. In the audio, the speaker uses the singular 'lavando a mão' colloquially, though the standard idiom is 'lavar as mãos'. It is a powerful idiom for advanced learners to describe someone avoiding accountability.

examples.en_text: I tried to help resolve the fight, but now I'm washing my hands of it.
examples.target_text: Eu tentei ajudar a resolver a briga, mas agora estou lavando as mãos.

examples.en_text: The manager washed his hands of the project's failure and blamed the team.
examples.target_text: O gerente lavou as mãos para o fracasso do projeto e culpou a equipe.

examples.en_text: You can't just wash your hands of the problem and pretend nothing happened.
examples.target_text: Você não pode simplesmente lavar as mãos e fingir que nada aconteceu.

examples.en_text: After so many lies, she is washing her hands of this relationship.
examples.target_text: Depois de tantas mentiras, ela está lavando as mãos dessa relação.

examples.en_text: If they don't want to listen to our advice, we are going to wash our hands of it.
examples.target_text: Se eles não querem ouvir nossos conselhos, nós vamos lavar as mãos.

examples.en_text: The politician washed his hands of the scandal, saying he knew nothing about it.
examples.target_text: O político lavou as mãos diante do escândalo, dizendo que não sabia de nada.

explanation_en: A highly common colloquial expression used to plead, emphasize a warning, or express exasperation. It translates literally to 'for the love of God' and is used in everyday spoken Portuguese across all social classes. It is crucial for learners to understand its emotional weight and natural usage in conversation.

examples.en_text: For God's sake, hurry up or we are going to miss the flight!
examples.target_text: Pelo amor de Deus, apresse-se ou vamos perder o voo!

examples.en_text: For God's sake, turn off that noisy music because I need to study.
examples.target_text: Pelo amor de Deus, desligue essa música barulhenta porque eu preciso estudar.

examples.en_text: Fifty reais for a coffee? For God's sake, that's a robbery!
examples.target_text: Cinquenta reais por um café? Pelo amor de Deus, isso é um roubo!

examples.en_text: For God's sake, tell me the truth once and for all.
examples.target_text: Pelo amor de Deus, me diga a verdade de uma vez por todas.

examples.en_text: Don't let the cat escape, for God's sake!
examples.target_text: Não deixe o gato escapar, pelo amor de Deus!

examples.en_text: For God's sake, when is it going to stop raining?
examples.target_text: Pelo amor de Deus, quando é que vai parar de chover?

explanation_en: This collocation combines 'saber' (to know / to be able to) with 'dizer' (to say / to tell). It is often used when acknowledging someone else's superior knowledge or authority on a subject, meaning 'to know enough to explain or confirm something'.

examples.en_text: I can't say for sure if the supermarket is still open at this hour.
examples.target_text: Não sei dizer se o supermercado ainda está aberto a esta hora.

examples.en_text: Can you tell me where the nearest bus stop is?
examples.target_text: Sabes dizer-me onde fica a paragem de autocarro mais próxima?

examples.en_text: He was so surprised that he couldn't say anything at the time.
examples.target_text: Ele ficou tão surpreso que não soube dizer nada na altura.

examples.en_text: The doctor still can't tell what the cause of the problem is.
examples.target_text: O médico ainda não sabe dizer qual é a causa do problema.

examples.en_text: If you ask me that tomorrow, maybe I'll be able to tell you by then.
examples.target_text: Se me perguntares isso amanhã, talvez eu já te saiba dizer.

examples.en_text: Sometimes it's hard to know how to say what we really want.
examples.target_text: Às vezes é difícil saber dizer o que realmente queremos.

explanation_en: This idiomatic expression means to present, discuss, or make something explicit in a discussion or analysis. It is equivalent to 'to bring to the table' or 'to lay cards on the table' in English, often used in debate, negotiation, or analytical contexts.

examples.en_text: We need to lay out all the options on the table before making a decision.
examples.target_text: Precisamos colocar todas as opções na mesa antes de tomar uma decisão.

examples.en_text: I think it's time to bring our differences to the table and talk.
examples.target_text: Acho que é hora de colocar as nossas diferenças na mesa e conversar.

examples.en_text: What can you bring to the table to help our company grow?
examples.target_text: O que você pode colocar na mesa para ajudar a nossa empresa a crescer?

examples.en_text: They finally brought the problem to the table and resolved the situation.
examples.target_text: Eles finalmente colocaram o problema na mesa e resolveram a situação.

examples.en_text: If you want to close the deal, put your best proposal on the table.
examples.target_text: Se você quer fechar o negócio, coloque a sua melhor proposta na mesa.

examples.en_text: I liked the ideas you brought to the table during today's meeting.
examples.target_text: Eu gostei das ideias que você colocou na mesa durante a reunião de hoje.

explanation_en: This phrase uses 'fazer algo com' to mean taking action or leveraging a situation/information that has arisen. It's a common way to describe reacting to a viral trend or piece of news by creating content or taking a specific step based on it.

examples.en_text: He inherited an old piece of land and finally did something with it.
examples.target_text: Ele herdou um terreno antigo e finalmente fez algo com isso.

examples.en_text: If you received that customer complaint, I hope you have already done something about it.
examples.target_text: Se você recebeu aquela reclamação do cliente, espero que já tenha feito algo com isso.

examples.en_text: We had a lot of wood piled up in the backyard and my brother did something with it.
examples.target_text: Nós tínhamos muita madeira acumulada no quintal e o meu irmão fez algo com isso.

examples.en_text: The government received the report on pollution and quickly did something about it.
examples.target_text: O governo recebeu o relatório sobre a poluição e rapidamente fez algo com isso.

examples.en_text: I had a suggestion to improve the office, and the boss actually did something about it.
examples.target_text: Eu tinha uma sugestão para melhorar o escritório, e o chefe realmente fez algo com isso.

examples.en_text: They had a great business opportunity and I'm glad they did something with it.
examples.target_text: Eles tinham uma grande oportunidade de negócio e fico feliz que tenham feito algo com isso.

explanation_en: The idiom 'chamar a atenção' means 'to attract attention' or 'to catch one's eye'. When followed by 'de' or a possessive pronoun, it specifies whose attention was caught. It is a fundamental expression in Portuguese, used across all registers.

examples.en_text: Of all the paintings in the gallery, which one caught your attention the most?
examples.target_text: De todos os quadros na galeria, qual foi o que chamou mais a tua atenção?

examples.en_text: In his resume, what caught your attention the most?
examples.target_text: No currículo dele, o que é que chamou mais a tua atenção?

examples.en_text: I liked the book, but the ending was what caught your attention the most, wasn't it?
examples.target_text: Eu gostei do livro, mas o final foi o que chamou mais a tua atenção, não foi?

examples.en_text: When you visited Lisbon, which monument caught your attention the most?
examples.target_text: Quando visitaste Lisboa, que monumento chamou mais a tua atenção?

examples.en_text: During yesterday's presentation, was there any detail that caught your attention the most?
examples.target_text: Durante a apresentação de ontem, houve algum detalhe que chamou mais a tua atenção?

examples.en_text: You were looking at the shop windows; which of those coats caught your attention the most?
examples.target_text: Estavas a olhar para as montras; qual daqueles casacos chamou mais a tua atenção?

explanation_en: This is a strong, formal way of saying 'absolutely not' or 'by no means'. It is synonymous with 'de jeito nenhum' but carries a slightly more polite or standard register, making it highly useful in both spoken and written Portuguese.

examples.en_text: Don't worry, you are not interrupting at all.
examples.target_text: Não se preocupe, você não está atrapalhando de forma nenhuma.

examples.en_text: By no means can we accept this proposal without reading the contract.
examples.target_text: De forma nenhuma podemos aceitar essa proposta sem ler o contrato.

examples.en_text: I didn't want to offend anyone, not at all.
examples.target_text: Eu não queria ofender ninguém, de forma nenhuma.

examples.en_text: Do you think it was a mistake to move cities? — Not at all, it was the best decision.
examples.target_text: Você acha que foi um erro mudar de cidade? — De forma nenhuma, foi a melhor decisão.

examples.en_text: The school rules do not allow, by any means, the use of cell phones during the exam.
examples.target_text: As regras da escola não permitem, de forma nenhuma, o uso de celulares durante a prova.

examples.en_text: She decided that, by no means, would she give up on her dreams.
examples.target_text: Ela decidiu que, de forma nenhuma, iria desistir dos seus sonhos.

explanation_en: This expression literally means 'behind the cameras' and is used metaphorically to mean 'behind the scenes' or 'off-camera/off-the-record'. It is commonly used in media, journalism, and everyday conversations to refer to things happening privately or out of public view.

examples.en_text: Behind the scenes, the actors are very good friends.
examples.target_text: Por trás das câmeras, os atores são muito amigos.

examples.en_text: There is a lot of hard work behind the scenes to make this show happen.
examples.target_text: Há muito trabalho duro por trás das câmeras para fazer este programa acontecer.

examples.en_text: Influencers' lives are not always perfect behind the scenes.
examples.target_text: A vida dos influenciadores nem sempre é perfeita por trás das câmeras.

examples.en_text: The reporter revealed what really happens behind the scenes of the news show.
examples.target_text: O repórter revelou o que realmente acontece por trás das câmeras do jornal.

examples.en_text: She prefers working behind the scenes rather than being the star of the movie.
examples.target_text: Ela prefere trabalhar por trás das câmeras do que ser a estrela do filme.

examples.en_text: The documentary shows the secrets and fights behind the scenes.
examples.target_text: O documentário mostra os segredos e as brigas por trás das câmeras.

explanation_en: The verb 'garantir' combined with the object pronoun 'te' (or 'lhe' in more formal contexts) is used to strongly emphasize the truth of an assertion. It is equivalent to 'I can assure you' or 'I can promise you' in English, conveying high confidence.

examples.en_text: I guarantee you that the restaurant is excellent, you will love it.
examples.target_text: Eu te garanto que o restaurante é excelente, você vai adorar.

examples.en_text: I can't guarantee you that the train will arrive on time because of the rain.
examples.target_text: Não posso te garantir que o trem vai chegar no horário por causa da chuva.

examples.en_text: Taking this course will guarantee you better job opportunities in the future.
examples.target_text: Fazer esse curso vai te garantir melhores oportunidades de emprego no futuro.

examples.en_text: No one can guarantee you that everything will work out, but we have to try.
examples.target_text: Ninguém pode te garantir que tudo vai dar certo, mas temos que tentar.

examples.en_text: The manager told me he was going to guarantee you a spot on the marketing team.
examples.target_text: O gerente me disse que ia te garantir uma vaga na equipe de marketing.

examples.en_text: If you study every day, I guarantee you that you will pass the exam.
examples.target_text: Se você estudar todos os dias, eu te garanto que vai passar na prova.
